notes.japanese: 畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて
notes.problem: The tautology reads as a mistake in English, not as emphasis; a reader stops to reparse it.
notes.span: every field that is a field, whether hemp or millet, has bowed its head limply in the earth-steam
notes.suggestion: every field worthy of the name, whether hemp or millet, has bowed its head limply in the earth-steam
notes.sureness: Fairly sure this is translationese; the desk's faithful reader can confirm the Japanese is idiomatic emphasis, not wordplay to preserve literally.

notes.japanese: 手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてある
notes.problem: "Handy" sounds like a评价 of usefulness, not size, and jars don't stand at pillows in English idiom.
notes.span: Then a handy unglazed jar stands at this man's pillow
notes.suggestion: Then a right-sized unglazed jar sits at this man's pillow
notes.sureness: Pretty sure "handy" is a false friend here; would settle by checking whether手ごろ means convenient-sized rather than useful.

notes.japanese: 七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる
notes.problem: "Posture of a turkey" plus "solemnly" is unintentionally comic and stiff; the contrast is the author's joke but the wording makes it machine-like.
notes.span: squats there solemnly, in the posture of a turkey
notes.suggestion: squats there with dignity, for all the world like a turkey
notes.sureness: Moderately sure; the humour is in the Japanese too, so keep the turkey, just make it sound like a writer wrote it.

notes.japanese: 踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである
notes.problem: "Rig" is modern slang and "hangs slovenly down" misuses an adjective as an adverb; the voice slips from Taisho-formal to nautical.
notes.span: his rig is a soap-black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels
notes.suggestion: his get-up is a soap-black cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot droops slovenlily
notes.sureness: Sure about "rig" and "slovenly" being wrong in this register; exact term for拵へ can be settled by the desk.

notes.japanese: 竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると
notes.problem: An English reader meets a person called a bamboo wife and a board-match described as fighting; both stop belief cold.
notes.span: leaning on his bamboo wife and fighting out a match on the board
notes.suggestion: leaning on his bamboo wife — a rattan bolster for hot nights — and battling out a game of go
notes.sureness: Very sure readers will picture a human wife; whether to gloss in-text or leave to context needs the editor's ruling on retained terms, but as it stands it misleads.

notes.japanese: 劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
notes.problem: The sentence breaks off on "as" with no main clause; it reads as a printing error, not authorial suspension.
notes.sureness: Certain this is incomplete in English; needs the desk to check if the continuation was lost in drafting — the Japanese runs on to the next speech.

notes.japanese: たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐる
notes.problem: The "that... or that..." apposition never resolves grammatically; the reader has to read twice to find the verb.
notes.span: that Chang San's black cataract suddenly took a turn for the better, for instance, or that Li Si's impotence was healed on the spot
notes.suggestion: how Chang San's black cataract suddenly took a turn for the better, for instance, or how Li Si's impotence was healed on the spot — rumours all but miraculous are rife
notes.sureness: Sure the syntax is broken in English; the fix keeps every fact and only repairs agreement.

notes.japanese: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
notes.problem: Second sentence has no subject in English, so it reads as a fragment rather than terse narration.
notes.span: And was himself ashamed of it.
notes.suggestion: And he was himself ashamed of it.
notes.sureness: Certain; joining or supplying the pronoun does not smooth any authorial roughness, only a drafting slip.

notes.japanese: 内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
notes.problem: Calling a person "absurd" is unidiomatic and the whole paragraph wobbles between present and past, formal and clumsy.
notes.span: he recalled within himself that his host Liu, who would meet such an arrogant monk, was absurd.
notes.suggestion: he thought his host Liu a fool for receiving such an arrogant monk.
notes.sureness: Pretty sure "was absurd" is dictionary English; tense consistency for the paragraph as a whole needs the desk to rule, but this clause is wrong on its own.

notes.japanese: 当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
notes.problem: Two opaque calques in one sentence: no English reader knows what "by the turn of the moment" or a "good friend on the wine-mound" is.
notes.span: That Sun Sensei, his good friend on the wine-mound, should by the turn of the moment stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
notes.suggestion: That Sun Sensei, his boon companion of the wine-mound, should as things fell out stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
notes.sureness: Sure "by the turn of the moment" means nothing in English; "wine-mound" still needs a light gloss on first use, which is an editor call under the keikaku test.

notes.japanese: 普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
notes.problem: The sly dig at schooling drowns in nominalization; "the doing of the same sort of thing" has a machine's habits, not a writer's.
notes.span: is in truth for the most part the doing of the same sort of thing.
notes.suggestion: is in truth for the most part doing much the same thing.
notes.sureness: Very sure; this keeps the narrator's digression intact and only removes the extra nouns.

notes.japanese: それでどこもかしこも、ぴりぴりする――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。
notes.problem: "A smarting everywhere" forces a verb into noun service; the ordeal passage needs to stay visceral, not grammatical puzzle.
notes.span: a pain that might best be described as a smarting everywhere.
notes.suggestion: a pain best described as a smarting all over.
notes.sureness: Sure the article + adverb fails in English; the oddness to keep is the clinical definition of pain, not the grammar.

notes.japanese: 曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。
notes.problem: "Doctored his soldiers' thirst" suggests falsifying it; the allusion misfires in English.
notes.span: doctored his soldiers' thirst by telling them there was a plum grove ahead.
notes.suggestion: cured his soldiers' thirst by telling them there was a plum grove ahead.
notes.sureness: Very sure "doctored" is wrong here; "cured" or "treated" preserves the ironic medical echo of医す — faithful reader to confirm nuance.

notes.japanese: 瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。
notes.problem: "Generously swollen" turns the jar jolly and purple; it ennobles a plain pot.
notes.span: perhaps half of its generously swollen belly.
notes.suggestion: perhaps half of its broadly swollen belly.
notes.sureness: Moderately sure;応揚 is dignified amplitude, not generosity — a plainer adjective keeps the erotic-thirsty gaze without the comedy.

notes.japanese: 何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらう
notes.problem: "Ridden on cajolery" mixes metaphors; no English speaker rides on cajolery into suffering.
notes.span: should have ridden on such a fellow's cajolery into this idiotic suffering.
notes.suggestion: should have let such a fellow's patter lead him into this idiotic suffering.
notes.sureness: Sure this is literal-translation idiom; the self-reproach and register stay, only the vehicle changes.

notes.japanese: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづつ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。
notes.problem: Standing the time-clause as its own fragment reads as an error, and "breast" for a fat man's chest confuses.
notes.suggestion: But at that very instant, Liu begins to feel an unnameable lump creeping little by little from his chest toward his throat.
notes.sureness: Sure the full stop after instant is a drafting chop of a long cumulative sentence the reading says to keep long; joining restores flow without prettifying.

notes.japanese: 蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて
notes.problem: "Haunches he had settled" is both indelicate and incomprehensible; a reader pictures animal hindquarters.
notes.span: lifts the haunches he had settled
notes.suggestion: heaves up the haunches he had settled himself upon
notes.sureness: Pretty sure the comedy is in the original turkey-squat, but "haunches" alone misleads; needs a plainer buttocks or a rephrase the desk approves.

notes.japanese: 長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。
notes.problem: "Three sun" means nothing to an English reader without help; it stops the climactic peer into the jar.
notes.span: It must be about three sun in length.
notes.suggestion: It must be about three sun — some four inches — in length.
notes.sureness: Certain an unexplained traditional unit fails the English reader; whether in-text gloss or note is an editor call, but it cannot stand bare — this is exactly the keikaku test.

data.say: The tableau and ordeal live, but dictionary diction, broken syntax and unexplained terms keep tripping the English reader.
